While in your starry form, you retain your game statistics, but your body becomes luminous; your joints glimmer like stars, et glowing lines connect them as on a star chart. This form sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius et dim light for an additional 10 feet. The form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), are {@condition incapacitated}, die, or use this feature again.
Whenever you assume your starry form, choose which of the following constellations glimmers on your body; your choice gives you certain benefits while in the form:

subclassFeatures.name: Archer
entries: A constellation of an archer appears on you. When you activate this form, et as a bonus action on your subsequent turns while it lasts, you can make a ranged spell attack, hurling a luminous arrow that targets one creature within 60 feet of you. On a hit, the attack deals radiant damage equal to {@damage 1d8} + your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeatures.name: Chalice
entries: A constellation of a life-giving goblet appears on you. Whenever you cast a spell using a spell slot that restores hit points to a creature, you or another creature within 30 feet of you can regain hit points equal to {@dice 1d8} + your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeatures.name: Dragon
entries: A constellation of a wise dragon appears on you. When you make an Intelligence or a Wisdom check or a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status concentration} on a spell, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the {@dice d20} as a 10.

subclassFeatures.name: Cosmic Omen
entries: {@i 6th-level Circle of the Stars feature}

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can consult your Star Map for omens. When you do so, roll a die. Until you finish your next long rest, you gain access to a special reaction based on whether you rolled an even or an odd number on the die:

items.name: Weal (even)
items.entry: Whenever a creature you can see within 30 feet of you is about to make an attack roll, a saving throw, or an ability check, you can use your reaction to roll a {@dice d6} et add the number rolled to the total.

items.name: Woe (odd)
items.entry: Whenever a creature you can see within 30 feet of you is about to make an attack roll, a saving throw, or an ability check, you can use your reaction to roll a {@dice d6} et subtract the number rolled from the total.

entries: You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, et you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Twinkling Constellations
entries: {@i 10th-level Circle of the Stars feature}
The constellations of your Starry Form improve. The {@damage 1d8} of the Archer et the Chalice becomes {@damage 2d8}, et while the Dragon is active, you have a flying speed of 20 feet et can hover.
Moreover, at the start of each of your turns while in your Starry Form, you can change which constellation glimmers on your body.

subclassFeatures.name: Full of Stars
entries: {@i 14th-level Circle of the Stars feature}
While in your Starry Form, you become partially incorporeal, giving you resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, et slashing damage.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of Wildfire
entries: Druides within the Circle of Wildfire understet that destruction is sometimes the precursor of creation, such as when a forest fire promotes later growth. These druids bond with a primal spirit that harbors both destructive et creative power, allowing the druids to create controlled flames that burn away one thing but give life to another.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle Spells
entries: {@i 2nd-level Circle of Wildfire feature}

You have formed a bond with a wildfire spirit, a primal being of creation et destruction. Your link with this spirit grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of Wildfire Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, et it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

subclassFeatures.name: Summon Wildfire Spirit
entries: {@i 2nd-level Circle of Wildfire feature}
You can summon the primal spirit bound to your soul. As an action, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape feature to summon your wildfire spirit, rather than assuming a beast form.

The spirit appears in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature within 10 feet of the spirit (other than you) when it appears must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take {@damage 2d6} fire damage.

The spirit is friendly to you et your companions et obeys your commets. See this creature's game statistics in the {@creature Wildfire Spirit|TCE} stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places. You determine the spirit's appearance. Some spirits take the form of a humanoid figure made of gnarled branches covered in flame, while others look like beasts wreathed in fire.

In combat, the spirit shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. The only action it takes on its turn is the {@action Dodge} action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to commet it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are {@condition incapacitated}, the spirit can take any action of its choice, not just {@action Dodge}.
The spirit manifests for 1 hour, until it is reduced to 0 hit points, until you use this feature to summon the spirit again, or until you die.

subclassFeatures.name: Enhanced Bond
entries: {@i 6th-level Circle of Wildfire feature}

The bond with your wildfire spirit enhances your destructive et restorative spells. Whenever you cast a spell that deals fire damage or restores hit points while your wildfire spirit is summoned, roll a {@dice d8}, et you gain a bonus equal to the number rolled to one damage or healing roll of the spell.
In addition, when you cast a spell with a range other than self, the spell can originate from you or your wildfire spirit.

subclassFeatures.name: Cauterizing Flames
entries: {@i 10th-level Circle of Wildfire feature}

You gain the ability to turn death into magical flames that can heal or incinerate. When a Small or larger creature dies within 30 feet of you or your wildfire spirit, a harmless spectral flame springs forth in the dead creature's space et flickers there for 1 minute. When a creature you can see enters that space, you can use your reaction to extinguish the spectral flame there et either heal the creature or deal fire damage to it. The healing or damage equals {@dice 2d10} + your Wisdom modifier.
You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, et you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Blazing Revival
entries: {@i 14th-level Circle of Wildfire feature}

The bond with your wildfire spirit can save you from death. If the spirit is within 120 feet of you when you are reduced to 0 hit points et thereby fall {@condition unconscious}, you can cause the spirit to drop to 0 hit points. You then regain half your hit points et immediately rise to your feet.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of the Blighted
entries: Those who channel the magic of life et nature often find themselves drawn to a particular shrine or natural site, binding their body et spirit to these places of power. Such druids draw vitality from their chosen location, protecting it with their lives—but not all succeed in defending these sacred realms.

Whether through the subtle corruption of vile magics, the tainted presence of an ancient terror, or a terrible mistake unleashed by druids themselves, a let can become cursed with magic that warps any druid bound to that let. Twisted by their connection to an unhallowed territory, these guardians come to embody the defiled nature they serve, exalting the natural process of decay et using it to further their goals—or sometimes to seek a means to end the curse that plagues them.

subclassFeatures.name: Blighted Shape
entries: Also at 2nd level, your physical form begins to show effects of the corruption you wield, tracing blackened veins across your skin, producing gnarled, bony protrusions, or other eerie phenomena. You gain proficiency in the Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) skill.

Additionally, while you are transformed by your Wild Shape feature, you gain a +2 bonus to AC as gnarled spines protrude from your body. Your beast form also gains {@sense darkvision} with a radius of 60 feet, or an additional 60 feet of {@sense darkvision} if it already has that sense.

subclassFeatures.name: Defile Ground
entries: Starting at 2nd level when you choose this circle, you can use a bonus action to corrupt a patch of let or an area of water in a 10-foot radius centered on a point within 60 feet of you. This corruption lasts for 1 minute. The corrupted area is {@quickref difficult terrain||3} for creatures that are hostile to you. Additionally, when a creature in the area takes damage from an attack or spell for the first time on a turn, it takes an extra {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage. You can move this patch of corruption up to 30 feet as a bonus action. Flying creatures are unaffected by the corruption.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.

subclassFeatures.name: Call of the Shadowseeds
entries: At 6th level, you learn to summon the feral children of the forest from the life force of your enemies. When a creature that is not undead or a construct takes damage within the area of your {@subclassFeature Defile Ground|Druid|PHB|Blighted|TDCSR|2} feature, you can use your reaction to summon a {@creature blighted sapling|TDCSR} in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the creature. You can direct the {@creature blighted sapling|TDCSR|sapling} to make an attack against any creature within 5 feet of it as a part of this reaction. The {@creature blighted sapling|TDCSR|sapling} then acts on your initiative, obeying your verbal commets.

The {@creature blighted sapling|TDCSR} remains in your service until it's reduced to 0 hit points, until the end of your next {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}, or until you summon another {@creature blighted sapling|TDCSR|sapling}, at which point it crumbles into foul-smelling mulch. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.
The {@creature blighted sapling|TDCSR|sapling} uses the statistics below. Its features scale based on your level et proficiency bonus (PB).

subclassFeatures.name: Defile Ground (10th Level)
entries: Starting at 10th level, the area of your defiled ground increases to a 20-foot radius. Additionally, the extra damage dealt by your defiled ground increases to {@damage 1d6} when you reach 10th level in this class.

subclassFeatures.name: Foul Conjuration
entries: Starting at 10th level, the creatures you conjure are malformed et bloated with toxins. Any beast, fey, or plant (including your {@creature blighted sapling|TDCSR}) summoned or created by your spells or class features gains the following traits:

entries.name: Blighted Resilience
entries: The creature has immunity to necrotic et poison damage et to the {@condition poisoned} condition.

entries.name: Toxic Demise
entries: When the creature is reduced to 0 hit points, it explodes in a burst of toxic mulch or fetid viscera. Each creature within 5 feet of the exploding creature must succeed on a Constitution {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} against your spell save DC or take necrotic damage based on the creature's challenge rating (see the table below). As an action, you can also cause a summoned creature to explode, immediately killing it.

entries.caption: Toxic Demise Damage
rows: {@damage (#$prompt_number:min=1,title=Enter the creature's CR!,default=1$#)d8|A number of d8s of necrotic damage equal to the creature's challenge rating}
{@damage (#$prompt_number:min=1,title=Enter your Proficiency Bonus!,default=1$#)d6|A number of d6s of necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus}

subclassFeatures.name: Defile Ground (14th Level)
entries: The extra damage dealt by your defiled ground increases to {@damage 1d8} when you reach 14th level in this class.

subclassFeatures.name: Incarnation of Corruption
entries: At 14th level, your physical form begins to take on the tainted traits of the let you are bonded to. Your skin grows ashen, et your eyes darken or turn completely white. Spines et jagged spurs emerge from your body, granting you resistance to necrotic damage et a +2 bonus to AC.

Additionally, whenever you start your turn within the radius of the corruption created by your {@subclassFeature Defile Ground|Druid|PHB|Blighted|TDCSR|2} feature, you can use a bonus action to gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of the Let
entries: {@i Celebrate Connection to the Natural World}

The Circle of the Let comprises mystics et sages who safeguard ancient knowledge et rites. These Druides meet within sacred circles of trees or steting stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of their communities.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of the Let Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24}, choose one type of let: arid, polar, temperate, or tropical. Consult the table below that corresponds to the chosen type; you have the spells listed for your Druide level et lower prepared.

entries.caption: Polar Let
rows: {@spell Fog Cloud|PHB24}, {@spell Hold Person|PHB24}, {@spell Ray of Frost|PHB24}

entries.caption: Tropical Let
rows: {@spell Acid Splash|PHB24}, {@spell Ray of Sickness|PHB24}, {@spell Web|PHB24}

subclassFeatures.name: Let's Aid
entries: As a {@action Magic|PHB24} action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape et choose a point within 60 feet of yourself. Vitality-giving flowers et life-draining thorns appear for a moment in a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Sphere} centered on that point. Each creature of your choice in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Sphere} must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. One creature of your choice in that area regains {@dice 2d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|PHB24}.
The damage et healing increase by {@dice 1d6} when you reach Druide levels 10 ({@dice 3d6}) et 14 ({@dice 4d6}).

subclassFeatures.name: Natural Recovery
entries: You can cast one of the level 1+ spells that you have prepared from your Circle Spells feature without expending a spell slot, et you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24} before you do so again.

In addition, when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|PHB24}, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your Druide level (round up), et none of them can be level 6+. For example, if you're a level 6 Druid, you can recover up to three levels' worth of spell slots. You can recover a level 3 spell slot, a level 2 et a level 1 spell slot, or three level 1 spell slots. Once you recover spell slots with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24}.

subclassFeatures.name: Nature's Ward
entries: You are immune to the {@condition Poisoned|PHB24} condition, et you have {@variantrule Resistance|PHB24} to a damage type associated with your current let choice in the Circle Spells feature, as shown in the {@skill Nature|PHB24}'s Ward table.

subclassFeatures.name: Nature's Sanctuary
entries: As a {@action Magic|PHB24} action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape et cause spectral trees et vines to appear in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Cube} on the ground within 120 feet of yourself. They last there for 1 minute or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|PHB24} condition or die. You et your allies have {@variantrule Cover|PHB24|Half Cover} while in that area, et your allies gain the current {@variantrule Resistance|PHB24} of your {@skill Nature|PHB24}'s Ward while there.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|PHB24}, you can move the {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Cube} up to 60 feet to ground within 120 feet of yourself.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle Forms
entries: You can channel lunar magic when you assume a Wild Shape form, granting you the benefits below.

entries.name: Challenge Rating
entries: The maximum {@variantrule Challenge Rating|PHB24} for the form equals your Druide level divided by 3 (round down).

entries.name: Armor Class
entries: Until you leave the form, your AC equals 13 plus your Wisdom modifier if that total is higher than the Beast's AC.

entries.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: You gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|PHB24} equal to three times your Druide level.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of the Moon
entries: {@i Adopt Animal Forms to Guard the Wilds}
Druides of the Circle of the Moon draw on lunar magic to transform themselves. Their order gathers under the moon to share news et perform rituals.

Changeable as the moon, a Druide of this circle might prowl as a great cat one night, soar over the treetops as an eagle the next day, et then crash through undergrowth as a bear to drive off a trespassing monster. The wild is in the Druid's blood.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of the Moon Spells
entries: When you reach a Druide level specified in the Circle of the Moon Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.
In addition, you can cast the spells from this feature while you're in a Wild Shape form.

subclassFeatures.name: Improved Circle Forms
entries: While in a Wild Shape form, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Lunar Radiance
entries: Each of your attacks in a Wild Shape form can deal its normal damage type or Radiant damage. You make this choice each time you hit with those attacks.

entries.name: Increased Toughness
entries: You can add your Wisdom modifier to your Constitution saving throws.

subclassFeatures.name: Moonlight Step
entries: You magically transport yourself, reappearing amid a burst of moonlight. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|PHB24}, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, et you have {@variantrule Advantage|PHB24} on the next attack roll you make before the end of this turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), et you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24}. You can also regain uses by expending a level 2+ spell slot for each use you want to restore (no action required).

subclassFeatures.name: Lunar Form
entries: The power of the moon suffuses you, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Improved Lunar Radiance
entries: Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 2d10} Radiant damage to a target you hit with a Wild Shape form's attack.

entries.name: Shared Moonlight
entries: Whenever you use Moonlight Step, you can also teleport one willing creature. That creature must be within 10 feet of you, et you teleport it to an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of your destination space.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of the Sea
entries: {@i Become One with Tides et Storms}

Druides of the Circle of the Sea draw on the tempestuous forces of oceans et storms. Some view themselves as embodiments of nature's wrath, seeking vengeance against those who despoil nature. Others seek mystical unity with nature by attuning themselves to the ebb et flow of the tides, following the rush of currents et waves et listening to the inscrutable whispers et roars of the winds.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of the Sea Spells
entries: When you reach a Druide level specified in the Circle of the Sea Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Circle of the Sea Spells
rows: {@spell Fog Cloud|PHB24}, {@spell Gust of Wind|PHB24}, {@spell Ray of Frost|PHB24}, {@spell Shatter|PHB24}, {@spell Thunderwave|PHB24}

subclassFeatures.name: Wrath of the Sea
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|PHB24}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to manifest a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Emanation} that takes the form of ocean spray that surrounds you for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), manifest it again, or have the {@condition Incapacitated|PHB24} condition.

When you manifest the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Emanation} et as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|PHB24} on your subsequent turns, you can choose another creature you can see in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Emanation}. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take Cold damage et, if the creature is Large or smaller, be pushed up to 15 feet away from you. To determine this damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one die).

subclassFeatures.name: Aquatic Affinity
entries: The size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Emanation} created by your Wrath of the Sea increases to 10 feet.
In addition, you gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|PHB24} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|PHB24}.

subclassFeatures.name: Stormborn
entries: Your Wrath of the Sea confers two more benefits while active, as detailed below.

entries.name: Flight
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|PHB24} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|PHB24}.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|PHB24} to Cold, Lightning, et Thunder damage.

subclassFeatures.name: Oceanic Gift
entries: Instead of manifesting the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Emanation} of Wrath of the Sea around yourself, you can manifest it around one willing creature within 60 feet of yourself. That creature gains all the benefits of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Emanation} et uses your spell save DC et Wisdom modifier for it.

In addition, you can manifest the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|PHB24|Emanation} around both the other creature et yourself if you expend two uses of your Wild Shape instead of one when manifesting it.

subclassFeatures.name: Circle of the Stars
entries: {@i Harness Secrets Hidden in Constellations}

The Circle of the Stars has tracked heavenly patterns since time immemorial, discovering secrets hidden amid the constellations. By understeting these secrets, the Druides of this circle seek to harness the powers of the cosmos.

subclassFeatures.name: Star Map
entries: You've created a star chart as part of your heavenly studies. It is a Tiny object, et you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|PHB24} for your Druide spells. You determine its form by rolling on the Star Map table or by choosing one.

While holding the map, you have the {@spell Guidance|PHB24} et {@spell Guiding Bolt|PHB24} spells prepared, et you can cast {@spell Guiding Bolt|PHB24} without expending a spell slot. You can cast it in that way a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), et you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24}.

If you lose the map, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to magically create a replacement. This ceremony can be performed during a {@variantrule Short Rest|PHB24|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24}, et it destroys the previous map.

entries.caption: Star Map
rows: A scroll bearing depictions of constellations
A stone tablet with fine holes drilled through it
An owlbear hide tooled with stellar symbols
A collection of maps bound in an ebony cover
A crystal engraved with starry patterns
A glass disk etched with constellations

subclassFeatures.name: Starry Form
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|PHB24}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to take on a starry form rather than shape-shifting.

While in your starry form, you retain your game statistics, but your body becomes luminous, your joints glimmer like stars, et glowing lines connect them as on a star chart. This form sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|PHB24} in a 10-foot radius et {@variantrule Dim Light|PHB24} for an additional 10 feet. The form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), have the {@condition Incapacitated|PHB24} condition, or use this feature again.
Whenever you assume your starry form, choose which of the following constellations glimmers on your body; your choice gives you certain benefits while in the form.

subclassFeatures.name: Archer
entries: A constellation of an archer appears on you. When you activate this form et as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|PHB24} on your subsequent turns while it lasts, you can make a ranged spell attack, hurling a luminous arrow that targets one creature within 60 feet of yourself. On a hit, the attack deals Radiant damage equal to {@damage 1d8} plus your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeatures.name: Chalice
entries: A constellation of a life-giving goblet appears on you. Whenever you cast a spell using a spell slot that restores {@variantrule Hit Points|PHB24} to a creature, you or another creature within 30 feet of you can regain {@variantrule Hit Points|PHB24} equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeatures.name: Dragon
entries: A constellation of a wise dragon appears on you. When you make an Intelligence or a Wisdom check or a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|PHB24}, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the {@dice d20} as a 10.

subclassFeatures.name: Cosmic Omen
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24}, you can consult your Star Map for omens et roll a die. Until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24}, you gain access to a special {@variantrule Reaction|PHB24} based on whether you rolled an even or an odd number on the die:

items.name: Weal (even)
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 30 feet of you is about to make a {@variantrule D20 Test|PHB24}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|PHB24} to roll {@dice 1d6} et add the number rolled to the total.

items.name: Woe (odd)
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 30 feet of you is about to make a {@variantrule D20 Test|PHB24}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|PHB24} to roll {@dice 1d6} et subtract the number rolled from the total.
You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|PHB24} a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), et you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|PHB24}.

subclassFeatures.name: Twinkling Constellations
entries: The constellations of your Starry Form improve. The {@damage 1d8} of the Archer et the Chalice becomes {@damage 2d8}, et while the Dragon is active, you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|PHB24} of 20 feet et can hover.
Moreover, at the start of each of your turns while in your Starry Form, you can change which constellation glimmers on your body.

subclassFeatures.name: Full of Stars
entries: While in your Starry Form, you become partially incorporeal, giving you {@variantrule Resistance|PHB24} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, et Slashing damage.

equipement: (a) a {@item mace|phb} or (b) a {@item warhammer|phb} (if proficient)
(a) {@item scale mail|phb}, (b) {@item leather armor|phb}, or (c) {@item chain mail|phb} (if proficient)
(a) a {@item light crossbow|phb} et {@item Crossbow Bolts (20)|phb|20 bolts} or (b) any {@filter simple weapon|items|source=phb|category=basic|type=simple weapon}
(a) a {@item priest's pack|phb} or (b) an {@item explorer's pack|phb}
A {@item shield|phb} et a {@item holy symbol|phb}

classFeatures.name: Incantation
entries: Vous avez appris à lancer des sorts par la prière et la méditation. Consultez le chapitre 7 pour connaître les règles relatives aux sorts. Les informations ci-dessous détaillent comment appliquer ces règles aux sorts de clerc, qui figurent dans la liste des sorts de clerc plus loin dans la description de la classe.

entries.name: Sorts mineurs
entries: Vous connaissez trois sorts mineurs de votre choix parmi la liste des sorts de clerc. {@spell Guidance}, {@spell Flamme sacrée} et {@spell Thaumaturgie} sont recommandés.
Chaque fois que vous gagnez un niveau de clerc, vous pouvez remplacer l'un de vos sorts mineurs par un autre sort mineur de votre choix dans la liste des sorts de clerc.

Lorsque vous atteignez les niveaux 4 et 10 de clerc, vous apprenez un autre sort mineur de votre choix dans la liste des sorts de clerc, comme indiqué dans la colonne Sorts mineurs du tableau des caractéristiques du clerc.

entries.name: Emplacements de sorts
entries: Le tableau des capacités du clerc indique le nombre d'emplacements de sorts dont vous disposez pour lancer vos sorts de niveau 1 et plus. Vous récupérez tous vos emplacements dépensés après un repos long.

entries.name: Sorts préparés de niveau 1 et plus
entries: Vous préparez la liste des sorts de niveau 1 et plus que vous pouvez lancer grâce à cette capacité. Pour commencer, choisissez quatre sorts de niveau 1 dans la liste des sorts de clerc. {@spell Bénédiction}, {@spell Soins des blessures}, {@spell Trait de lumière} et {@spell Bouclier de la foi} sont recommandés.

Le nombre de sorts de votre liste augmente à mesure que vous gagnez des niveaux de clerc, comme indiqué dans la colonne « Sorts préparés » du tableau des aptitudes de clerc. À chaque augmentation de ce nombre, choisissez des sorts supplémentaires dans la liste de sorts de clerc jusqu'à ce que votre liste de sorts corresponde à celle du tableau. Les sorts choisis doivent être d'un niveau pour lequel vous disposez d'emplacements de sorts. Par exemple, si vous êtes un clerc de niveau 3, votre liste de sorts préparés peut inclure six sorts de niveaux 1 et 2, dans n'importe quelle combinaison.

Si une autre capacité de clerc vous donne des sorts que vous avez toujours préparés, ces sorts ne sont pas comptabilisés dans le nombre de sorts que vous pouvez préparer avec cette capacité, mais ils sont par ailleurs considérés comme des sorts de clerc.

entries.name: Modification de vos sorts préparés
entries: Lorsque vous terminez un repos long, vous pouvez modifier votre liste de sorts préparés, en remplaçant n'importe quel sort par d'autres sorts de clerc pour lesquels vous disposez d'emplacements de sorts.

entries.name: Capacité d'incantation
entries: La Sagesse est votre caractéristique d'incantation pour vos sorts de clerc.

entries.name: Focalisation de sorts
entries: Vous pouvez utiliser un symbole sacré comme focalisateur de sorts pour vos sorts de clerc.

classFeatures.name: Ordre Divin
entries: Vous vous êtes consacré à l'un des rôles sacrés suivants, de votre choix.

entries.name: Protecteur
entries: Entraîné au combat, vous acquérez la maîtrise des armes martiales et l'entraînement au maniement des armures lourdes.

entries.name: Thaumaturge
entries: Vous connaissez un sort mineur supplémentaire de la liste de sorts de clerc. De plus, votre lien mystique avec le divin vous confère un bonus à vos tests d'Intelligence ( Arcanes ou Religion ). Ce bonus est égal à votre modificateur de Sagesse (minimum +1).

classFeatures.name: Canalisation divine
entries: Vous pouvez canaliser l'énergie divine directement depuis les Plans Extérieurs pour alimenter des effets magiques. Vous commencez avec deux effets de ce type : Étincelle Divine et Repousser les Morts-Vivants, décrits ci-dessous. Chaque fois que vous utilisez Canalisation Divine de cette classe, choisissez l'effet de Canalisation Divine à créer. Vous obtenez des options d'effets supplémentaires aux niveaux de Clerc supérieurs.

Vous pouvez utiliser le Canal divin de cette classe deux fois. Vous récupérez une utilisation dépensée après un repos court et toutes les utilisations dépensées après un repos long. Vous obtenez des utilisations supplémentaires en atteignant certains niveaux de clerc, comme indiqué dans la colonne Canal divin du tableau des capacités de clerc.
Si un effet de Canalisation divine nécessite un jet de sauvegarde, le DD est égal au DD de sauvegarde du sort provenant de la capacité de lancement de sorts de cette classe.

entries.name: Étincelle divine
entries: Par une action magique, vous pointez votre Symbole sacré vers une créature visible à moins de 9 mètres et concentrez votre énergie divine sur elle. Lancez 1d8 et ajoutez votre modificateur de Sagesse. Vous restaurez alors à la créature un nombre de points de vie égal au résultat du jet de sauvegarde de Constitution. En cas d'échec, la créature subit des dégâts nécrotiques ou radiants (à votre choix) égaux au résultat du jet de sauvegarde. En cas de réussite, elle subit la moitié des dégâts (arrondi à l'inférieur).

entries.name: Repousser les morts-vivants
entries: Par une action magique, vous présentez votre symbole sacré et censurez les créatures mortes-vivantes. Chaque mort-vivant de votre choix situé à moins de 9 mètres de vous doit effectuer un jet de sauvegarde de Sagesse. En cas d'échec, la créature est effrayée et incapable d'agir pendant 1 minute. Durant cette durée, elle tente de s'éloigner le plus possible de vous à chaque tour. Cet effet prend fin prématurément si la créature subit des dégâts, si vous êtes incapable d'agir ou si vous mourez.

classFeatures.name: Sous-classe de clerc
entries: Vous obtenez une sous-classe de clerc de votre choix. Une sous-classe est une spécialisation qui vous confère des capacités à certains niveaux de clerc. Pour le reste de votre carrière, vous bénéficiez de toutes les capacités de votre sous-classe correspondant à votre niveau de clerc ou à un niveau inférieur.

classFeatures.name: Amélioration de caractéristique
entries: Vous recevez le don {@feat Amélioration de caractéristique|PHB24} ou un autre {@5etools don|feats.html} de votre choix pour lequel vous remplissez les condition. Vous recevez de nouveau cette aptitude aux niveau de Bard 8, 12, and 16.

classFeatures.name: Brûler les morts-vivants
entries: Lorsque vous utilisez Repousser les morts-vivants, vous pouvez lancer un nombre de d8 égal à votre modificateur de Sagesse (minimum 1d8 ) et additionner les résultats. Chaque mort-vivant qui rate son jet de sauvegarde contre cette utilisation de Repousser les morts-vivants subit des dégâts radiants égaux au total du jet. Ces dégâts ne mettent pas fin à l'effet de Repousser les morts-vivants.

classFeatures.name: Capacité de sous-classe
entries: Vous obtenez une capacité de votre sous-classe de clerc.

classFeatures.name: Frappes bénies
entries: La puissance divine vous imprègne au combat. Vous obtenez l'une des options suivantes, au choix (si vous obtenez l'une des options d'une sous-classe de clerc dans un ouvrage plus ancien, utilisez uniquement celle que vous avez choisie pour cette capacité).

entries.name: Frappe divine
entries: Une fois par tour, lorsque vous touchez une créature avec un jet d'attaque utilisant une arme, vous pouvez infliger à la cible 1d8 dégâts nécrotiques ou radiants supplémentaires (à votre choix).

entries.name: Incantation puissante
entries: Ajoutez votre modificateur de Sagesse aux dégâts infligés par n'importe quel sort mineur de clerc.

classFeatures.name: Amélioration de caractéristique
entries: Vous recevez le don {@feat Amélioration de caractéristique|PHB24} ou un autre {@5etools don|feats.html} de votre choix pour lequel vous remplissez les condition.

classFeatures.name: Intervention divine
entries: Vous pouvez invoquer votre divinité ou votre panthéon pour qu'il intervienne en votre faveur. Par une action magique, choisissez un sort de clerc de niveau 5 ou inférieur qui ne nécessite pas de réaction. Au cours de cette même action, vous lancez ce sort sans dépenser d'emplacement de sort ni utiliser de composantes matérielles. Vous ne pouvez pas réutiliser cette capacité avant d'avoir terminé un repos long.

classFeatures.name: Amélioration de caractéristique
entries: Vous recevez le don {@feat Amélioration de caractéristique|PHB24} ou un autre {@5etools don|feats.html} de votre choix pour lequel vous remplissez les condition.

classFeatures.name: Frappes bénies améliorées
entries: L'option que vous avez choisie pour Frappes bénies devient plus puissante.

entries.name: Frappe divine
entries: Les dégâts supplémentaires de votre Frappe divine passent à 2d8.

entries.name: Incantation puissante
entries: Lorsque vous lancez un sort mineur de clerc et infligez des dégâts à une créature, vous pouvez vous octroyer de la vitalité ou en octroyer à une autre créature située à moins de 18 mètres de vous, en lui accordant un nombre de points de vie temporaires égal à deux fois votre modificateur de Sagesse.

classFeatures.name: Amélioration de caractéristique
entries: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeatures.name: Capacité de sous-classe
entries: Vous obtenez une capacité de votre sous-classe de clerc.

classFeatures.name: Bénédiction épique
entries: Vous obtenez un don de  {@filter Don épique feat|feats|category=EB} ou un autre {@5etools don|feats.html}de votre choix pour lequel vous remplissez les conditions requises. Le {@feat Don du Destin|PHB24} de sorts est recommandé.

classFeatures.name: Intervention divine supérieure
entries: Vous pouvez faire appel à une intervention divine encore plus puissante. Lorsque vous utilisez votre capacité Intervention divine, vous pouvez choisir le sort {@spell Souhait} lors de la sélection d'un sort. Dans ce cas, vous ne pourrez plus utiliser Intervention divine avant d'avoir effectué 2d4 repos longs.

subclassFeatures.name: Knowledge Domain
entries: The gods of knowledge—including {@deity Oghma}, {@deity Boccob|Greyhawk}, {@deity Gilean|Dragonlance}, {@deity Aureon|Eberron}, et {@deity Thoth|Egyptian}—value learning et understeting above all. Some teach that knowledge is to be gathered et shared in libraries et universities, or promote the practical knowledge of craft et invention. Some deities hoard knowledge et keep its secrets to themselves. et some promise their followers that they will gain tremendous power if they unlock the secrets of the multiverse. Followers of these gods study esoteric lore, collect old tomes, delve into the secret places of the earth, et learn all they can. Some gods of knowledge promote the practical knowledge of craft et invention, including smith deities like {@deity Gond}, {@deity Reorx|Dragonlance}, {@deity Onatar|Eberron}, {@deity Moradin|Nonhuman}, {@deity Hephaestus|Greek}, et {@deity Goibhniu|Celtic}.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessings of Knowledge
entries: At 1st level, you learn two languages of your choice. You also become proficient in your choice of two of the following skills: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}.
Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those skills.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to tap into a divine well of knowledge. As an action, you choose one skill or tool. For 10 minutes, you have proficiency with the chosen skill or tool.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
entries: At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to read a creature's thoughts. You can then use your access to the creature's mind to commet it.

As an action, choose one creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature succeeds on the saving throw, you can't use this feature on it again until you finish a long rest.

If the creature fails its save, you can read its surface thoughts (those foremost in its mind, reflecting its current emotions et what it is actively thinking about) when it is within 60 feet of you. This effect lasts for 1 minute.

During that time, you can use your action to end this effect et cast the {@spell suggestion} spell on the creature without expending a spell slot. The target automatically fails its saving throw against the spell.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Strikes
entries: {@i 8th-level cleric {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}, which replaces the Potent Spellcasting feature}

You are blessed with divine might in battle. When a creature takes damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to that creature. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeatures.name: Potent Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

subclassFeatures.name: Visions of the Past
entries: Starting at 17th level, you can call up visions of the past that relate to an object you hold or your immediate surroundings. You spend at least 1 minute in meditation et prayer, then receive dreamlike, shadowy glimpses of recent events. You can meditate in this way for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score et must maintain {@status concentration} during that time, as if you were casting a spell.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Object Reading
entries: Holding an object as you meditate, you can see visions of the object's previous owner. After meditating for 1 minute, you learn how the owner acquired et lost the object, as well as the most recent significant event involving the object et that owner. If the object was owned by another creature in the recent past (within a number of days equal to your Wisdom score), you can spend 1 additional minute for each owner to learn the same information about that creature.

entries.name: Area Reading
entries: As you meditate, you see visions of recent events in your immediate vicinity (a room, street, tunnel, clearing, or the like, up to a 50-foot cube), going back a number of days equal to your Wisdom score. For each minute you meditate, you learn about one significant event, beginning with the most recent. Significant events typically involve powerful emotions, such as battles et betrayals, marriages et murders, births et funerals. However, they might also include more mundane events that are nevertheless important in your current situation.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
Life Domain
entries: The Life domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy—one of the fundamental forces of the universe—that sustains all life. The gods of life promote vitality et health through healing the sick et wounded, caring for those in need, et driving away the forces of death et undeath. Almost any non-evil deity can claim influence over this domain, particularly agricultural deities (such as {@deity Chauntea}, {@deity Arawai|Eberron}, et {@deity Demeter|Greek}), sun gods (such as {@deity Latheter}, {@deity Pelor|Greyhawk}, et {@deity Re-Horakhty|Egyptian}), gods of healing or endurance (such as {@deity Ilmater}, {@deity Mishakal|Dragonlance}, {@deity Apollo|Greek}, et {@deity Diancecht|Celtic}), et gods of home et community (such as {@deity Hestia|Greek}, {@deity Hathor|Egyptian}, et {@deity Boldrei|Eberron}).
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

subclassFeatures.name: Disciple of Life
entries: Also starting at 1st level, your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to heal the badly injured.

As an action, you present your holy symbol et evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level. Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, et divide those hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on an undead or a construct.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Healer
entries: Beginning at 6th level, the healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Strikes
entries: {@i 8th-level cleric {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}, which replaces the Divine Strike feature}

You are blessed with divine might in battle. When a creature takes damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to that creature. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeatures.name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeatures.name: Supreme Healing
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring {@dice 2d6} hit points to a creature, you restore 12.

subclassFeatures.name: Light Domain
entries: Gods of light—including {@deity Helm}, {@deity Latheter}, {@deity Pholtus|Greyhawk}, {@deity Branchala|Dragonlance}, {@deity the Silver Flame|Eberron}, {@deity Belenus|Celtic}, {@deity Apollo|Greek}, et {@deity Re-Horakhty|Egyptian}—promote the ideals of rebirth et renewal, truth, vigilance, et beauty, often using the symbol of the sun. Some of these gods are portrayed as the sun itself or as a charioteer who guides the sun across the sky. Others are tireless sentinels whose eyes pierce every shadow et see through every deception. Some are deities of beauty et artistry, who teach that art is a vehicle for the soul's improvement. Clerics of a god of light are enlightened souls infused with radiance et the power of their gods' discerning vision, charged with chasing away lies et burning away darkness.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

entries.caption: Light Domain Spells
rows: {@spell guardian of faith}, {@spell wall of fire}

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Cantrip
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain the {@spell light} cantrip if you don't already know it. This cantrip doesn't count against the number of cleric cantrips you know.

subclassFeatures.name: Warding Flare
entries: Also at 1st level, you can interpose divine light between yourself et an attacking enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker before it hits or misses. An attacker that can't be {@condition blinded} is immune to this feature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to harness sunlight, banishing darkness et dealing radiant damage to your foes.

As an action, you present your holy symbol, et any magical darkness within 30 feet of you is dispelled. Additionally, each hostile creature within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes radiant damage equal to {@damage 2d10} + your cleric level on a failed saving throw, et half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that has {@quickref Cover||3||total cover} from you is not affected.

subclassFeatures.name: Improved Flare
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can also use your Warding Flare feature when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you attacks a creature other than you.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Strikes
entries: {@i 8th-level cleric {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}, which replaces the Potent Spellcasting feature}

You are blessed with divine might in battle. When a creature takes damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to that creature. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeatures.name: Potent Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

subclassFeatures.name: Corona of Light
entries: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to activate an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius et dim light 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
Nature Domain
entries: Gods of nature are as varied as the natural world itself, from inscrutable gods of the deep forests (such as {@deity Silvanus}, {@deity Obad-Hai|Greyhawk}, {@deity Chislev|Dragonlance}, {@deity Balinor|Eberron}, et {@deity Pan|Greek}) to friendly deities associated with particular springs et groves (such as {@deity Eldath}). Druids revere nature as a whole et might serve one of these deities, practicing mysterious rites et reciting all-but-forgotten prayers in their own secret tongue. But many of these gods have clerics as well, champions who take a more active role in advancing the interests of a particular nature god. These clerics might hunt the evil monstrosities that despoil the woodlets, bless the harvest of the faithful, or wither the crops of those who anger their gods.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Acolyte of Nature
entries: At 1st level, you learn one druid cantrip of your choice. This cantrip doesn't count against the number of cleric cantrips you know. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Animal Hetling}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Survival}.

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: Also at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals et Plants
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to charm animals et plants.

As an action, you present your holy symbol et invoke the name of your deity. Each beast or plant creature that can see you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is {@condition charmed} by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage. While it is {@condition charmed} by you, it is friendly to you et other creatures you designate.

subclassFeatures.name: Dampen Elements
entries: Starting at 6th level, when you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to the creature against that instance of the damage.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Strikes
entries: {@i 8th-level cleric {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}, which replaces the Divine Strike feature}

You are blessed with divine might in battle. When a creature takes damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to that creature. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeatures.name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} cold, fire, or lightning damage (your choice) to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeatures.name: Master of Nature
entries: At 17th level, you gain the ability to commet animals et plant creatures. While creatures are {@condition charmed} by your Charm Animals et Plants feature, you can take a bonus action on your turn to verbally commet what each of those creatures will do on its next turn.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals et Plants
Channel Divinity: Charm Animals et Plants
Tempest Domain
entries: Gods whose portfolios include the Tempest domain—including {@deity Talos}, {@deity Umberlee}, {@deity Kord|Greyhawk}, {@deity Zeboim|Dragonlance}, {@deity the Devourer|Eberron}, {@deity Zeus|Greek}, et {@deity Thor|Norse}—govern storms, sea, et sky. They include gods of lightning et thunder, gods of earthquakes, some fire gods, et certain gods of violence, physical strength, et courage. In some pantheons, a god of this domain rules over other deities et is known for swift justice delivered by thunderbolts. In the pantheons of seafaring people, gods of this domain are ocean deities et the patrons of sailors. Tempest gods send their clerics to inspire fear in the common folk, either to keep those folk on the path of righteousness or to encourage them to offer sacrifices of propitiation to ward off divine wrath.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons et heavy armor.

subclassFeatures.name: Wrath of the Storm
entries: Also at 1st level, you can thunderously rebuke attackers. When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to cause the creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. The creature takes {@damage 2d8} lightning or thunder damage (your choice) on a failed saving throw, et half as much damage on a successful one.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to wield the power of the storm with unchecked ferocity.
When you roll lightning or thunder damage, you can use your Channel Divinity to deal maximum damage, instead of rolling.

subclassFeatures.name: Thunderbolt Strike
entries: At 6th level, when you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Strikes

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} thunder damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeatures.name: Stormborn
entries: At 17th level, you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed whenever you are not underground or indoors.

subclassFeatures.name: Trickery Domain
entries: Gods of trickery—such as {@deity Tymora}, {@deity Beshaba}, {@deity Olidammara|Greyhawk}, {@deity the Traveler|Eberron}, {@deity Garl Glittergold|Nonhuman}, et {@deity Loki|Norse}—are mischief-makers et instigators who stet as a constant challenge to the accepted order among both gods et mortals. They're patrons of thieves, scoundrels, gamblers, rebels, et liberators. Their clerics are a disruptive force in the world, puncturing pride, mocking tyrants, stealing from the rich, freeing captives, et flouting hollow traditions. They prefer subterfuge, pranks, deception, et theft rather than direct confrontation.
At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessing of the Trickster
entries: Starting when you choose this domain at 1st level, you can use your action to touch a willing creature other than yourself to give it advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks. This blessing lasts for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to create an illusory duplicate of yourself.

As an action, you create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 1 minute, or until you lose your {@status concentration} (as if you were {@status concentration||concentrating} on a spell). The illusion appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move the illusion up to 30 feet to a space you can see, but it must remain within 120 feet of you.

For the duration, you can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, but you must use your own senses. Additionally, when both you et your illusion are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature, given how distracting the illusion is to the target.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to vanish.
As an action, you become {@condition invisible} until the end of your next turn. You become visible if you attack or cast a spell.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Strikes
entries: {@i 8th-level cleric {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}, which replaces the Divine Strike feature}

You are blessed with divine might in battle. When a creature takes damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to that creature. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeatures.name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with poison—a gift from your deity. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} poison damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeatures.name: Improved Duplicity
entries: At 17th level, you can create up to four duplicates of yourself, instead of one, when you use Invoke Duplicity. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move any number of them up to 30 feet, to a maximum range of 120 feet.

subclassFeatures.name: War Domain
entries: War has many manifestations. It can make heroes of ordinary people. It can be desperate et horrific, with acts of cruelty et cowardice eclipsing instances of excellence et courage. In either case, the gods of war watch over warriors et reward them for their great deeds. The clerics of such gods excel in battle, inspiring others to fight the good fight or offering acts of violence as prayers. Gods of war include champions of honor et chivalry (such as {@deity Torm}, {@deity Heironeous|Greyhawk}, et {@deity Kiri-Jolith|Dragonlance}) as well as gods of destruction et pillage (such as {@deity Erythnul|Greyhawk}, {@deity the Fury|Eberron}, {@deity Gruumsh|Nonhuman}, et {@deity Ares|Greek}) et gods of conquest et domination (such as {@deity Bane}, {@deity Hextor|Greyhawk}, et {@deity Maglubiyet|Nonhuman}). Other war gods (such as {@deity Tempus}, {@deity Nike|Greek}, et {@deity Nuada|Celtic}) take a more neutral stance, promoting war in all its manifestations et supporting warriors in any circumstance.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons et heavy armor.

subclassFeatures.name: War Priest
entries: From 1st level, your god delivers bolts of inspiration to you while you are engaged in battle. When you use the {@action Attack} action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to strike with supernatural accuracy. When you make an attack roll, you can use your Channel Divinity to gain a +10 bonus to the roll. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing
entries: At 6th level, when a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to the roll, using your Channel Divinity. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage of the same type dealt by the weapon to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeatures.name: Avatar of Battle
entries: At 17th level, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, et slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

subclassFeatures.name: Death Domain
entries: The Death domain is concerned with the forces that cause death, as well as the negative energy that gives rise to undead creatures. Deities such as {@deity Chemosh|Dragonlance}, {@deity Myrkul}, et {@deity Wee Jas|Greyhawk} are patrons of necromancers, death knights, liches, mummy lords, et vampires. Gods of the Death domain also embody murder ({@deity Anubis|Egyptian}, {@deity Bhaal}, et Pyremius), pain ({@deity Iuz|Greyhawk} or {@deity Loviatar}), disease or poison ({@deity Incabulos|Greyhawk}, {@deity Talona}, or {@deity Morgion|Dragonlance}), et the underworld ({@deity Hades|Greek} et {@deity Hel|Norse}).
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared. They do not count towards your limit.

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: When the cleric chooses this domain at 1st level, he or she gains proficiency with martial weapons.

subclassFeatures.name: Reaper
entries: At 1st level, the cleric learns one {@filter necromancy cantrip|spells|level=0|school=N} of his or her choice from any spell list. When the cleric casts a necromancy cantrip that normally targets only one creature, the spell can instead target two creatures within range et within 5 feet of each other.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Touch of Death
entries: Starting at 2nd level, the cleric can use Channel Divinity to destroy another creature's life force by touch.
When the cleric hits a creature with a melee attack, the cleric can use Channel Divinity to deal extra necrotic damage to the target. The damage equals 5 + twice his or her cleric level.

subclassFeatures.name: Inescapable Destruction
entries: Starting at 6th level, the cleric's ability to channel negative energy becomes more potent. Necrotic damage dealt by the character's cleric spells et Channel Divinity options ignores resistance to necrotic damage.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Strikes
entries: {@i 8th-level cleric {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}, which replaces the Divine Strike feature}

You are blessed with divine might in battle. When a creature takes damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to that creature. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeatures.name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, the cleric gains the ability to infuse his or her weapon strikes with necrotic energy. Once on each of the cleric's turns when he or she hits a creature with a weapon attack, the cleric can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage to the target. When the cleric reaches 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeatures.name: Improved Reaper
entries: Starting at 17th level, when the cleric casts a Necromancy spell of 1st through 5th-level that targets only one creature, the spell can instead target two creatures within range et within 5 feet of each other. If the spell consumes its material components, the cleric must provide them for each target.

subclassFeatures.name: Arcana Domain
entries: Magic is an energy that suffuses the multiverse et that fuels both destruction et creation. Gods of the Arcana domain know the secrets et potential of magic intimately. For some of these gods, magical knowledge is a great responsibility that comes with a special understeting of the nature of reality. Other gods of Arcana see magic as pure power, to be used as its wielder sees fit.

The gods of this domain are often associated with knowledge, as learning et arcane power tend to go het-in-het. In the Realms, deities of this domain include {@deity Azuth|Faerûnian|SCAG} et {@deity Mystra|Faerûnian|SCAG}, as well as {@deity Corellon Larethian|Elven|SCAG} of the elven pantheon. In other worlds, this domain includes {@deity Hecate|Greek}, {@deity Math Mathonwy|Celtic}, et {@deity Isis|Egyptian}; the triple moon gods of {@deity Solinari|Dragonlance}, {@deity Lunitari|Dragonlance}, et {@deity Nuitari|Dragonlance} of Krynn; et {@deity Boccob|Greyhawk}, {@deity Vecna|Greyhawk}, et {@deity Wee Jas|Greyhawk} of Greyhawk.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared. They do not count towards your limit.

subclassFeatures.name: Arcane Initiate
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana} skill, et you gain two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter wizard spell list|spells|class=wizard|level=0}. For you, these cantrips count as cleric cantrips.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Arcane Abjuration
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to abjure otherworldly creatures.

As an action, you present your holy symbol, et one celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend of your choice that is within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw, provided that the creature can see or hear you. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, et it can't willingly end its move in a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the {@action Dash} action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, then the creature can use the {@action Dodge} action.

After you reach 5th level, when a creature fails its saving throw against your Arcane Abjuration feature, the creature is banished for 1 minute (as in the {@spell banishment} spell, no {@status concentration} required) if it isn't on its plane of origin, et its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold, as shown below.

subclassFeatures.name: Spell Breaker
entries: Starting at 6th level, when you restore hit points to an ally with a spell of 1st level or higher, you can also end one spell of your choice on that creature. The level of the spell you end must be equal to or lower than the level of the spell slot you use to cast the healing spell.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessed Strikes
entries: {@i 8th-level cleric {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}, which replaces the Potent Spellcasting feature}

You are blessed with divine might in battle. When a creature takes damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to that creature. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeatures.name: Potent Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

subclassFeatures.name: Arcane Mastery
entries: At 17th level, you choose four spells from the Wizard spell list, one from each of the following levels: 6th, 7th, 8th, et 9th. You add them to your list of domain spells. Like your other domain spells, they are always prepared et count as cleric spells for you.

subclassFeatures.name: Ambition Domain (PSA)

entries: The worthy shall strive for greatness—supremacy in life leads to supremacy in the afterlife.

Bontu has fully embraced this dictum, et though she expends little effort in teaching it, she surely leads by example. Her viziers subtly plant the seeds that flower into the ambition the God-Pharaoh desires. Through insinuation, they remind acolytes et initiates alike that achieving one's place in the afterlife at the expense of others is not shameful, but is proof of the initiate's determination et drive. Nothing is more important than that drive, they suggest—not the bonds of a crop, not friendship or love. Not even devotion to a deity.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Warding Flare
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you can interpose divine light between yourself et an attacking enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker before it hits or misses. An attacker that can't be {@condition blinded} is immune to this feature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Knowledge Domain (PSA)

entries: The worthy shall cultivate a nimble mind that can perceive the wonders beyond imagination that wait in the afterlife.

Kefnet's task is to pass on this teaching of the God-Pharaoh et elucidate its meaning. He teaches that the afterlife will be inhabited only by those who have proved by their wits that they are worthy of dwelling in the glorious presence of the God-Pharaoh. He trains acolytes et initiates to push their limits et challenge their mental capacity with spells of ever-greater power.
Kefnet's domain is identical to the {@class Cleric|PHB|Knowledge domain in the Player's Hetbook|Knowledge|PHB}.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
Solidarity Domain (PSA)

entries: The worthy must know et respect all others whom the God-Pharaoh deems worthy, for in the afterlife, all will be united in purpose et action.

Oketra is charged with expounding upon this teaching of the God-Pharaoh, instilling in every initiate the virtue of solidarity. She forges each group of children into a crop of acolytes with just one purpose: to be judged worthy of a glorious afterlife. et she instills in each crop the ability to unite in a single action in pursuit of that purpose. She is fond of poetic imagery to communicate her ideals.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

entries.caption: Solidarity Domain Spells
rows: {@spell aura of life}, {@spell guardian of faith}
{@spell circle of power}, {@spell mass cure wounds}

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

subclassFeatures.name: Solidarity's Action
entries: Also at 1st level, when you take the {@action Help} action to aid an ally's attack, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to heal the badly injured.

As an action, you present your holy symbol et evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level. Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, et divide those hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on an undead or a construct.

entries: At 6th level, when a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to the roll, using your Channel Divinity. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

subclassFeatures.name: Supreme Healing
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring {@dice 2d6} hit points to a creature, you restore 12.

subclassFeatures.name: Strength Domain (PSA)

entries: The worthy shall hone a strong body that can withstet the boundless energies of the afterlife.

It falls to Rhonas to instill this teaching in those who would enter the afterlife—but to his mind, the words themselves don't matter. Strength can't be taught. It must be built through practice et training. Rhonas demonstrates his teachings by his example, rather than by giving his students any kind of academic instruction. He welcomes the people of Naktamun to stet by the Hekma et watch him as he storms into the desert to battle the greatest horrors. He encourages them to observe his indomitable strength, for though they will never equal it, they can aspire to mimicry. He invites them to scrutinize every move et practice what they see.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Acolyte of Strength
entries: At 1st level, you learn one druid cantrip of your choice. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Animal Hetling}, {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Survival}.

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: Also at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

subclassFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Feat of Strength
entries: At 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to enhance your physical might. When you make an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw using Strength, you can use your Channel Divinity to gain a +10 bonus to the roll. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the roll succeeds or fails.

subclassFeatures.name: Rhonas's Blessing
entries: At 6th level, when a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw using Strength, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to the roll, using your Channel Divinity. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the roll succeeds or fail.

entries: At 17th level, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, et slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

subclassFeatures.name: Zeal Domain (PSA)

entries: The worthy shall rush to the God-Pharaoh's side with relentless zeal, rising to overcome every obstacle in their way.

The God-Pharaoh expects those he welcomes into the afterlife to desire it above all other pleasures et achievements, et for them to show their dedication, passion, et fervor through their actions. Hazoret is charged with cultivating this zeal in the initiates who come under her care, et she has undertaken the task with appropriate enthusiasm. She recognizes, however, that the best way to teach zeal is by demonstrating it.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

entries.caption: Zeal Domain Spells
rows: {@spell fire shield||fire shield (warm shield only)}, {@spell freedom of movement}

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons et heavy armor.

entries: From 1st level, Hazoret delivers bolts of inspiration to you while you are engaged in battle. When you use the {@action Attack} action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

When you roll fire or thunder damage, you can use your Channel Divinity to deal maximum damage instead of rolling.

When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeatures.name: Blaze of Glory
entries: Starting at 17th level, you can delay death for an instant to perform a final heroic act.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points by an attacker you can see, even if you would be killed outright, you can use your reaction to move up to your speed toward the attacker et make one melee weapon attack against it, as long as the movement brings it within your reach. You make this attack with advantage. If the attack hits, the creature takes an extra {@damage 5d10} fire damage et an extra {@damage 5d10} damage of the weapon's type. You then fall {@condition unconscious} et begin making death saving throws as normal, or you die if the damage you took would have killed you outright.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Forge Domain
entries: The gods of the forge are patrons of artisans who work with metal, from a humble blacksmith who keeps a village in horseshoes et plow blades to the mighty elf artisan whose diamond-tipped arrows of mithral have felled demon lords. The gods of the forge teach that, with patience et hard work, even the most intractable metal can be transformed from a lump of ore to a beautifully wrought object. Clerics of these deities search for objects lost to the forces of darkness, liberate mines overrun by orcs, et uncover rare et wondrous materials necessary to create potent magic items. Followers of these gods take great pride in their work, et they are willing to craft et use heavy armor et powerful weapons to protect them. Deities of this domain include {@deity Gond}, {@deity Reorx|Dragonlance}, {@deity Onatar|Eberron}, {@deity Moradin|Nonhuman}, {@deity Hephaestus|Greek}, et {@deity Goibhniu|Celtic}.
At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared.

subclassFeatures.name: Blessing of the Forge
entries: At 1st level, you gain the ability to imbue magic into a weapon or armor. At the end of a long rest, you can touch one nonmagical object that is a suit of armor or a {@filter simple or martial weapon|items|source=phb|category=basic|type=martial weapon;simple weapon}. Until the end of your next long rest or until you die, the object becomes a magic item, granting a +1 bonus to AC if it's armor or a +1 bonus to attack et damage rolls if it's a weapon.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiency
